_note: Seed 3 rolls a Thief Pickpocket Human — a normal (non-Troll/Elven/Dwarven) race so priceFor's multipliers don't complicate the arithmetic, and a class that can legally buy every weapon/armor slot openStore might roll. The test bumps state.c.gold to 5000 identically on BOTH the prototype and engine sides right after boot (before opening the store) so the scenario can afford a full spread of purchase categories (food/potion/weapon/armor/premium/lockpicks) and still land on a genuine insufficient-gold case at the end — openStore itself is deterministic from the seed, so this gold bump changes nothing about which stock rolls, only what's affordable. 'openStore'/'buyItem'/'leaveStore' indices below were hand-verified against this exact seed's rolled stock (see test/parity/economy-parity.test.js's harness note). A top-level `divergence` record (kind action-path, fromAction 0, stockCostMul 1.25) is declared for this fixture's Pickpocket hero (Phase 24, IDENT-05/FID-07): the store roll is proven byte-identical to the prototype while gold, weapon, and items diverge because every routed store line costs 1.25x more, making the Set-of-lockpicks and Katana purchases (actions 6-7) unaffordable on the engine side two purchases before the prototype runs dry.

divergence.rationale: The seed-3 hero is a Human Pickpocket; Phase 24 marks up every priceFor-routed store line (buyWeapon/buyArmor/buyPremium/buyRations/repairArmor) x1.25 for a Pickpocket, floor 1. Phase 39 (GEAR-01) re-prices the WEAPONS table itself, so a flat multiplier off the PROTOTYPE's own cost no longer describes the engine's line prices (the prototype is frozen at Katana 525/Axe 50/Broadsword-premium 500; the engine now sells Katana 650, Broadsword 550, before the 1.25x Pickpocket markup) — the stockCostMul check is replaced by the stronger stockNames/stockAfter pin: the store ROLL is still byte-identical to the prototype (same 12 names, in order — Rations is the engine's own extra line, excluded from stockNames and present only in stockAfter) while every routed cost is measured directly. With the same 5000-gold bump on both sides, the higher engine prices no longer starve the run the way the old prices did: the engine now affords everything the prototype does PLUS extra purchases the prototype's own gold ran out before reaching (the fixture's own action order buys Axe/Studded/Casket/Lockpicks/Katana/Speed potion in sequence) — action 5 (Casket, 4128) still fails on both sides (both are far short of a ~4100-gold premium item at this point), but the engine ends the script with 2066 gold left over (vs the prototype's 55) and a Speed potion the prototype could never reach. `weaponUpgradeDelta`'s new expected-strike heuristic also makes the Axe purchase (action 3) a takeItem 'notBetter' rejection on BOTH sides (the Pickpocket's starting Dagger already out-crits a bare Axe) — gold is still spent (the store always deducts on a legal purchase attempt), so this does not change the declared fields. Seed/actions/gold bump are deliberately untouched — the divergence is declared, not dodged. Purchase mechanics parity for a non-Pickpocket hero is unchanged code (buyFrom/takeItem/sellItem's arithmetic paths are untouched for a non-Pickpocket sub) and is covered instead by test/unit/economy.test.js's priceFor/sellPriceFor/seed-3-stock-pin cases.
